title: Quantum-Classical Framework for the Joint Optimization of Bidirectional EV Charging and Trip Assignment
authors: Mustafa Musab, Sebastian Schmitt, Markus Wappler, Jörg Lässig, Daniel Müssig
abstract: The integration of bidirectional (V2G) charging allows electric vehicle (EV) fleets to operate as distributed energy assets. However, the joint optimization of charging schedules and trip assignments is NP-hard. Moreover, bidirectional power flows create non-monotonic state-of-charge (SoC) dynamics that weaken standard dual-based Benders cuts. We propose a hybrid quantum-classical Benders decomposition framework. To overcome the qubit overhead associated with encoding feasibility cuts, we introduce logic-based conflict cuts, which require near-zero auxiliary qubits. Furthermore, we develop a sparse recursive SoC formulation that reduces the constraint-matrix density by a factor of T/3 in the horizon length T. We demonstrate that our framework recovers MILP-optimal solutions on benchmark instances with a low auxiliary-qubit budget, and, as a minimal proof of concept, we execute a small instance end-to-end on IBM quantum hardware.
summary: This paper tackles the complex, NP-hard problem of optimizing EV charging and trip assignments using a novel hybrid quantum-classical approach. It introduces a Benders decomposition framework that uses logic-based cuts to minimize quantum overhead, alongside a recursive formulation to drastically reduce model size. The method is validated by achieving near-optimal solutions on benchmarks and running a small test case on actual quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the NP-hard joint optimization problem of scheduling electric vehicle (EV) trips and managing bidirectional charging (V2G).
main_result: A hybrid quantum-classical Benders decomposition framework is proposed that successfully recovers MILP-optimal solutions on benchmarks using a low auxiliary-qubit budget.
method: It combines Benders decomposition, using logic-based conflict cuts to reduce qubit overhead, with a sparse recursive SoC formulation for model size reduction.
model_or_system: The system models EV fleets with bidirectional charging capabilities, formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) solved via a Master Problem (MP) on a quantum computer (QAOA) and a classical Subproblem (SP).
key_observables: Benders convergence gap, relative gap compared to direct MILP, and the number of non-zero elements (nnz) in the constraint matrix.
important_parameters: Time horizon (T), number of EVs (N_EV), maximum charging power (l_max), and the required final State-of-Charge (E_min^n).
main_assumptions: The logic-based cut method assumes the grid power capacity is sufficient, and the quantum encoding relies on mapping constraints to penalty terms in the Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process of extracting Irreducible Inconsistent Subsystems (IIS) to generate combinatorial conflict cuts, and tables compare the performance of the hybrid Benders approach against direct MILP solvers.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the NP-hard problem, details the hybrid Benders decomposition, presents the novel sparse recursive SoC formulation, and validates the framework by showing convergence on benchmark instances and executing a proof-of-concept on IBM quantum hardware.
why_interesting: While the application is in optimization/power systems, the core methodology involves mapping complex combinatorial constraints into quantum circuits (QAOA) and developing quantum-aware decomposition techniques, which is relevant to quantum algorithm development for constrained optimization.
